Subject: Private fleet upgrade: scope, pinning policy & rollback validation

Hannah —

Thanks for the call earlier. We need to lock in the maintenance window and the specific rollback criteria for our private deployment (VPC, customer-controlled network). A few asks from our side so we can complete change approval at Acme: 

- Confirm Redwood's recommended version pinning behavior for private (can we pin to major+minor, and who performs the fast rollback if pinned?)
- Maintenance window proposal: 2026-09-22 02:00-06:00 UTC (low traffic) — ok?
- We need a written rollback checklist that our on-call can run with NOC runbook links and expected RTO/RPO targets.
- Any mandatory network-side steps (BGP flap mitigation, NAT gateway checks) we should schedule with our NetOps team?

If you can send a short plan and a copy of your rollback checklist, we'll route it through our platform change board. Attachment from our side: "acme-netops-constraints.pdf" (referenced).

Thanks,
Priya Chang
Head of Cloud Operations — Acme Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade: scope, pinning policy & rollback validation

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the summary. Briefly: the plan below reflects our recommended defaults for private customers and the exceptions we can support for Acme. I've attached a small runbook draft (private-upgrade-runbook-v1.2.pdf) and will circulate the more detailed checklist after internal sign-off.

High level:
- Version pinning: by default we pin to MAJOR.MINOR for private (e.g., 2.7). Customers may opt into automatic patch channel (2.7.x) for minor security fixes — but only after you approve the patch window. For this upgrade, we'll treat it as a manual minor bump (no auto-roll).
- Maintenance window: 2026-09-22 02:00-06:00 UTC is acceptable from Redwood's side. We'll reserve a 4-hour window with a 60-minute cool-down and a 2-hour extended rollback hold period.
- Rollback ownership: Redwood will provide the rollback procedure; Acme's on-call executes the network-side actions (we'll provide exact commands). If rollback is triggered due to performance regressions or data path errors, Redwood SRE (cc: soojin) will coordinate execution with your NOC.
- Network precautions: please schedule BGP dampening thresholds and NAT gateway failover tests with NetOps; we'll provide a pre-cutover checklist for NetOps to run.

Next steps: soojin, can you draft the executable rollback checklist (to attach) and add canary-gating thresholds? Karthik/Naomi — please confirm the pinning policy wording and the exact sequence for pin/unpin.

I'll update Acme once we've got internal approvals.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Chang <p.chang@acmehealth.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade: scope, pinning policy & rollback validation

Hannah / all —

Draft rollback checklist (summary) — I'll attach as "rollback-checklist.md" and include a machine-readable CSV template for canary metrics. Full doc will be uploaded to the shared Drive. Key items: 

1) Pre-cutover (T-48h):
   - Snapshot model versions and KV caches. Verify snapshot integrity (sha256).
   - Confirm NetOps readiness: BGP dampening set to conservative values; NAT gateway warm spares healthy.
   - Canary cluster reserved (10% of traffic) with telemetry baseline recorded.

2) Cutover sequence (T+0):
   - Pause background batch jobs that mutate model state.
   - Deploy new runtime to canary slice (isolate routing). Run smoke tests (3x successful inference runs with golden prompts).
   - Evaluate canary metrics: 95th-latency, error-rate, token-loss; fail if deviation > 20%/absolute error-rate > 0.5%.

3) Rollback criteria (explicit triggers):
   - Canary fail condition (above) OR 
   - Network path degradation (packet loss > 1% for > 5 minutes) OR
   - Persistent backend GC/oom events.

4) Rollback execution (T+N):
   - Step A: Switch routing for canary back to previous version and hold for 15 minutes.
   - Step B: If stable, stage progressive un-deploy on next tranche; if unstable, execute fleet-wide rollback using snapshot restore procedure.
   - Step C: Open incident, assign RCA lead, schedule postmortem.

5) Post-rollback validation:
   - Run synthetic traffic runbook (attached) and confirm RTO target: 30 minutes for canary isolation, 3 hours for full fleet restore.

Notes: I'll include exact kubectl/hfctl commands and config snippets in the attached checklist. Connor, please confirm the snapshot restore timeline (we currently estimate ~2.5 hours for full KV restore on the Acme fleet size).

Thanks — attaching: "rollback-checklist.md", "canary-metrics-template.csv"

— Soojin
Soojín Lee
SRE, Private Runtime

- Maintenance window: 2026-09-22 02:00-06:00 UTC with a 60m cool-down and 2h rollback hold.
- Canary gating: Soojin's thresholds (95th latency + error-rate) as pass/fail; template attached (canary-metrics-template.csv).

Attachments: private-upgrade-runbook-v1.2.pdf (contains sequence + commands), rollback-checklist.md, canary-metrics-template.csv.

Action items for Acme: please confirm NetOps time block for NAT/BGP checks and acknowledge the RTO targets by EOD 2026-09-15 so we can finalize change board package.

If you want, we can do a 30-minute dry-run on 2026-09-20 to rehearse the rollback sequence with your NOC.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
